chapter_summary: Before His arrest, Jesus prays to the Father about His completed mission, His disciples, and future believers. He asks that they be kept in truth, made holy, united, and filled with divine love.
main_lesson: Jesus shares eternal glory with the Father and gives eternal life through knowing God. He prays for His people to live in truthful, safe unity and to bear witness while remaining in the world.

memory_verse.kjv: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
memory_verse.little_bible: And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.

parent_guide: Access: default for ages 6–8 and 9–12 with adult context; ages 3–5 receive curated verses such as 3, 8, 13, 17, 20–21, and 26. Sensitivity: approaching crucifixion and death, eternal life, chosen/kept/lost language and Judas, hatred and opposition, spiritual protection, mission, institutional unity, exclusion, and complex Trinitarian and union language. Glory through the cross never makes suffering or death desirable. Eternal life affirms relationship with God and never invites death. Judas must not create anxiety that ordinary mistakes prove a child is lost. Protection is not guaranteed physical safety. “World” language permits no contempt. Mission never requires stranger evangelism. Unity never requires forced reconciliation, secrecy, or unsafe institutions. Spiritual union is not physical merging or private voices. God’s love is given, not earned.
application_for_children: Children may receive Jesus’ prayer as hopeful care, ask questions, value earthly life, remain truthful, respect neighbours, witness only in safe age-appropriate ways, keep protective boundaries, and seek trusted help when afraid or harmed.

verses.kjv: These words spake Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:
verses.little_bible: Jesus spoke these words, lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son also may glorify you,
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus prayed for the Father to glorify the Son, who would glorify the Father.
verses.meaning: Jesus approaches the cross as his appointed “hour” and asks that his obedient death, resurrection, and exaltation reveal Father and Son. Glory does not make death desirable or invite a child to seek suffering.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can the cross reveal love without making suffering desirable?
verses.family_discussion: Name ways to honour Jesus’ sacrifice while protecting life.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally draw a cross surrounded by signs of life and hope.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:1, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him.
verses.little_bible: as you have given him authority over all people, so that he should give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father gave Jesus authority to give eternal life to those given to him.
verses.meaning: The Father gives the Son authority over all humanity so he may give eternal life to those the Father has given him. Christians differ on how ‘given’ relates to election, foreknowledge, faith, and salvation’s scope; the verse gives no warrant to classify particular children as excluded. Jesus’ authority serves life rather than coercion.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus use his authority to give?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss authority that serves and gives rather than controls.
verses.do_it_today: Use one responsibility today to help rather than control.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:2, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
verses.little_bible: And this is eternal life: that they might know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Eternal life is knowing the true God and Jesus Christ, whom he sent.
verses.meaning: Eternal life is relational knowledge of the Father through Jesus Christ, the sent Son. Calling the Father ‘the only true God’ does not deny the Son’s deity: this same prayer presents the Son as sharing the Father’s glory before creation. Eternal life begins now and never invites a child to seek death.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why is eternal life more than simply living after death?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm that earthly life and care remain precious while discussing eternal hope.
verses.do_it_today: Enjoy one safe part of life and thank God for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:3, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
verses.little_bible: I have glorified you on the earth: I have finished the work which you gave me to do.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus completed the work the Father gave him.
verses.meaning: Jesus looks ahead to the completion of his earthly mission. His unique finished work is not a productivity standard by which children earn worth.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How is Jesus’ unique mission different from a child’s achievement list?
verses.family_discussion: Celebrate faithful effort without tying worth to completion.
verses.do_it_today: Stop one task for rest without calling yourself a failure.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:4, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
verses.little_bible: And now, Father, glorify me with you, with the glory I had with you before the world existed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked to share again the glory he had with the Father before creation.
verses.meaning: The Son asks to return to the glory shared with the Father before creation. This supports Christ’s pre-existence and divine identity while distinguishing Father and Son.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does this prayer tell us about Jesus before creation?
verses.family_discussion: Use two distinct circles to represent Father and Son sharing glory.
verses.do_it_today: Look at the night sky and remember Jesus existed before creation.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:5, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word.
verses.little_bible: I have made your name known to the people whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me; and they have kept your word.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus revealed the Father to the people given to him, and they kept God’s word.
verses.meaning: Jesus has made the Father known to the disciples entrusted to him. Their keeping of the word is evidence of reception, not perfect performance or the price of being chosen.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why does receiving love come before faithful response?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss grace before obedience and growth after reception.
verses.do_it_today: Receive a kind word without trying to repay it.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:6, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee.
verses.little_bible: Now they have known that everything you have given me comes from you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples knew Jesus’ gifts came from the Father.
verses.meaning: The disciples recognize that Jesus’ mission, teaching, and gifts come from the Father. Their understanding remains real though incomplete.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What had the disciples begun to understand?
verses.family_discussion: Trace what comes from the Father across verses 6–8.
verses.do_it_today: Circle each gift from the Father in the verse.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:7, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me.
verses.little_bible: For I have given them the words you gave me; and they have received them, and have known truly that I came from you, and they have believed that you sent me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They received the Father’s words and believed the Father sent Jesus.
verses.meaning: The disciples receive Jesus’ words, know his divine origin, and believe his sending. Faith here rests on revelation, not coerced certainty.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What helped the disciples believe Jesus was sent?
verses.family_discussion: Welcome one faith question without forcing certainty.
verses.do_it_today: Retell one apostolic word about Jesus accurately.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:8, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.
verses.little_bible: I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for they are yours.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, ‘I pray for these disciples, not for the world here. They belong to the Father.’
verses.meaning: Jesus’ immediate focus is intercession for his disciples, not a statement that he never cares or prays for the world; elsewhere his mission expresses God’s love for the world.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why should this verse not mean Jesus has no care for others?
verses.family_discussion: Read John 3:16 alongside this focused prayer.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, pray for both the church and the wider world. You may pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:9, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them.
verses.little_bible: And all mine are yours, and yours are mine; and I am glorified in them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Father and Son share all things, and Jesus was glorified in the disciples.
verses.meaning: Father and Son mutually possess all things, and Jesus’ character is displayed through his disciples. This is unique divine communion, not interchangeable identities.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What does this verse show about Father and Son?
verses.family_discussion: List shared language without erasing Father-Son distinction.
verses.do_it_today: Use separate colours for Father and Son references.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:10, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.
verses.little_bible: And now I am no longer in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to you. Holy Father, keep in your own name those whom you have given me, so that they may be one, as we are.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus was returning to the Father while the disciples stayed in the world. He asked the Father to keep them in his name and make them one.
verses.meaning: Jesus asks the Holy Father to guard disciples who remain amid danger and to unite them. Divine keeping does not guarantee freedom from physical harm; unity never requires unsafe access or silence about wrongdoing.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can unity include safety, truth, and difference?
verses.family_discussion: Review that reconciliation requires truth, accountability, and safety.
verses.do_it_today: Help two safe people cooperate without hiding disagreement.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:11, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.
verses.little_bible: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I have kept those whom you gave me, and none of them is lost except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus guarded the disciples; Judas was lost as Scripture had said.
verses.meaning: Jesus preserved the apostolic group entrusted to him, yet Judas—the ‘son of perdition’—followed the path that fulfilled Scripture. Christians differ on whether Judas exemplifies apostasy, a false disciple never savingly included, or a unique apostolic judgment. The verse must never make children think anxiety or an ordinary mistake proves they are secretly doomed.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What reassurance helps when this verse creates fear about being lost? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Reassure children that anxiety or mistakes do not make them Judas; no disclosure is needed.
verses.do_it_today: Say, “Jesus receives anxious learners,” or simply pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:12, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
verses.little_bible: And now I come to you; and I speak these things in the world so that they might have my joy made full in themselves.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus spoke so his joy would be fulfilled in the disciples.
verses.meaning: Jesus speaks openly so his disciples may share his joy. Joy can accompany grief and fear; it is not forced cheerfulness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can joy and grief exist together?
verses.family_discussion: Make room for one joyful and one difficult feeling.
verses.do_it_today: Choose one gentle source of joy while allowing sadness.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:13, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
verses.little_bible: I have given them your word; and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The world hated the disciples because they no longer belonged to its way.
verses.meaning: “The world” here means humanity organized in resistance to God, not every outsider, Jewish person, or non-Christian neighbour. Opposition never permits contempt.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why does “world” not mean every person outside church?
verses.family_discussion: Practise respectful words for neighbours of different beliefs.
verses.do_it_today: With an adult, greet a known safe neighbour respectfully across a difference.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:14, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.
verses.little_bible: I do not pray that you would take them out of the world, but that you would keep them from the evil.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked the Father to keep them from the evil one while they remained in the world.
verses.meaning: Jesus asks the Father to guard disciples while they remain in society and mission. The phrase is translated as protection from ‘evil’ or ‘the evil one’; both readings concern divine keeping, not guaranteed physical safety or a reason to ignore practical help.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What should believers still do when physical danger appears?
verses.family_discussion: Review trusted adults and safety steps; spiritual trust complements practical help.
verses.do_it_today: Write two safe-help contacts with an adult, or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:15, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
verses.little_bible: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples did not belong to the world’s rebellious way.
verses.meaning: The repeated contrast concerns allegiance to the world’s rebellion, not withdrawal from ordinary people or treating culture and creation as worthless.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can disciples live among neighbours without sharing every value?
verses.family_discussion: Plan one friendly interaction across a difference.
verses.do_it_today: If you wish, join one safe community activity with a trusted adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:16, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
verses.little_bible: Make them holy through your truth. Your word is truth.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus asked the Father to make them holy through his true word.
verses.meaning: To sanctify is to set apart for God’s holy purpose through divine truth. God’s word is the standard; sanctification is not perfectionism, shame, or forced disclosure.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How does truth make people holy without shaming them?
verses.family_discussion: Compare truthful formation with shame or secret-demanding pressure.
verses.do_it_today: Check one claim against Jesus’ recorded words.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:17, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.
verses.little_bible: As you have sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus sent the disciples into the world as the Father sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus commissions the apostles as the Father commissioned him. Children should witness through truthful, age-appropriate life with adult support—not approach strangers or enter unsafe situations.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What is a safe, age-appropriate way to represent Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Choose witness among known people with adult knowledge, never stranger contact.
verses.do_it_today: With a parent or trusted adult’s knowledge, share one truth about Jesus only with someone known, safe, and willing—or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:18, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.
verses.little_bible: And for their sake I set myself apart, so that they also might be made holy through the truth.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus set himself apart so they would be made holy in truth.
verses.meaning: Jesus consecrates himself to the Father’s saving mission, especially the cross, so the disciples are consecrated in truth. His unique sacrifice is not a demand for children to endanger themselves.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why is Jesus’ self-giving mission unique?
verses.family_discussion: State clearly that self-endangerment does not imitate Jesus.
verses.do_it_today: Protect your own and others’ safety in one small way.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:19, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word;
verses.little_bible: I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who will believe in me through their word,
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus also prayed for future believers who would trust their message.
verses.meaning: Jesus’ prayer reaches future believers through the apostles’ message, grounding the church’s faith in their testimony rather than private revelation.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Whose message leads later believers to faith?
verses.family_discussion: Thank God for reliable apostolic testimony.
verses.do_it_today: Show gratitude for apostolic testimony by reading one Gospel paragraph with an adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:20, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
verses.little_bible: that they all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you; that they also may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus prayed that believers would be united in Father and Son, so the world might believe the Father sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus prays for relational unity that reflects Father and Son and supports witness. Unity preserves distinction and truth; it never requires forced reconciliation with abusers or submission to unsafe institutions.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why can unity never require return to an unsafe person?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss a disagreement that can remain honest without hostility.
verses.do_it_today: Practise a safe boundary while still speaking kindly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:21, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one:
verses.little_bible: And the glory which you gave me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one:
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus shared glory with believers so they might be one.
verses.meaning: Christians variously understand the shared glory here as God’s revealed presence, cross-shaped mission, participation in Christ’s life, or the honour of belonging to him. Whatever its precise emphasis, it serves believers’ unity and does not make them divine by nature, erase individuality, or grant status over others.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: What kind of unity preserves each person?
verses.family_discussion: Build something united from distinct pieces.
verses.do_it_today: Make a mosaic from different pieces that stay visible.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:22, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.
verses.little_bible: I in them, and you in me, so that they may be brought into complete unity; and so that the world may know that you have sent me and have loved them as you have loved me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus prayed, ‘I in them and you in me,’ so believers would be united and the world would know the Father sent and loved them.
verses.meaning: The Father in the Son and Christ in believers describes spiritual communion, not physical merging or private voices. Their truthful unity supports witness, and the Father’s love reaches them through Christ; the comparison does not erase the Son’s unique identity, give believers identical intra-Trinitarian status, or make love something they earn.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How is spiritual union different from physical merging or private voices?
verses.family_discussion: Use linked rings that remain separate to picture communion.
verses.do_it_today: Link paper rings without blending them into one.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:23, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
verses.little_bible: Father, I desire that those whom you have given me may also be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you have given me; for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus wanted his disciples with him to see his glory, given because the Father loved him before the world began.
verses.meaning: Jesus desires his people to be with him and behold his pre-creation glory. This hope must not romanticize death, pressure grieving children, or suggest earthly life is disposable.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why must eternal hope never encourage someone to seek death? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: If grief is present, allow silence and passing without spiritual pressure.
verses.do_it_today: Choose life-giving care if this verse raises thoughts of death; tell a safe adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:24, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.
verses.little_bible: O righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these people have known that you sent me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus knew the righteous Father, and the disciples knew the Father sent him.
verses.meaning: Jesus contrasts the world’s failure to know the righteous Father with his own knowledge and the disciples’ recognition of his mission. It is not permission for contempt.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: How can conviction and respect for others remain together?
verses.family_discussion: Practise conviction without insults or superiority.
verses.do_it_today: Ask one honest question without mocking another person.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:25, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.

verses.kjv: And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare it: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them.
verses.little_bible: And I have made your name known to them, and will make it known, so that the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I in them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus made the Father known so the Father’s love for Jesus would be in believers, and Jesus would be in them.
verses.meaning: Jesus continues revealing the Father so the Father’s love for the Son may dwell in believers and Christ may dwell in them. Believers participate in this love by grace; they do not become the Son by nature, earn love through performance, or receive compulsory private voices.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me receive your prayer with truth, hope, and safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why is God’s love gift rather than wages?
verses.family_discussion: Receive love without listing accomplishments.
verses.do_it_today: Rest for a moment in the truth that love is given.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 17:26, Jesus praying with disciples nearby under gentle lamplight, historically appropriate, non-graphic, no text.
